summary: Round-2 fleet knife, measured: fuse reclaim into one atomic critical section (supersede + mint successor) so racing reclaims can never leave a phantom second active lease; add CAS crash recovery via expected_generation (exactly one winner, losers get LeaseConflictError); refuse acquire on a live active lease; declare optional lease ttl_seconds with renew_lease and the only time-licensed takeover path reclaim_if_expired (unexpired/expiry-free leases refuse with LeaseActiveError so live takeover stays an explicit operator reclaim); fuse project/workspace find-or-create against coordinator-boot TOCTOU.

components.owning_subsystem: durable fleet registry lease lifecycle (disk-only authority under the existing cross-process fcntl lock)
components.disposition: ADMIT as the round-2 tranche of the already-declared fleet control machinery. The program owns only mechanical race/expiry facts: lease generations, atomic supersede, CAS, declared expiries. Whether to take over a live unexpired lease stays a model/operator decision (refused mechanically).
evidence: Round-1 reclaim was two lock steps (supersede, then a separate acquire): two racing reclaims could interleave so the second acquire minted a fresh active generation on top of an active lease, leaving two active leases in durable state.
acquire_lease accepted a live active current without superseding it - a silent takeover hole.
WorkerLease had no expiry fact at all; a crashed worker's workspace could only be recovered at the same run boundary by begin_run, never by another owner on a time basis.

ProjectCoordinator boot used get->create TOCTOU for the project record: two concurrent coordinators crashed the loser with KeyError (observed as a deadlocked test barrier, reproduced deterministically).
components.verification_level: RED-first race/expiry suite (real filesystem, real elapsed time, thread hammer via separate flock descriptors, cross-process subprocess hammer), adjacent fleet gates, Ruff, Pyright, full non-real_llm pytest, A.5 self-check
components.model_evidence_veto_recovery_exit: Every refusal is a typed mechanical fact (LeaseConflictError / LeaseActiveError with remaining-seconds or no-expiry reason). An operator can still take over any live lease through the explicit reclaim path; reclaim_if_expired only licenses takeover by declared expiry, never by semantic judgment. Coordinator recover() exposes expires_at and expired as facts for model/operator judgment.
components.rollback_route: Revert the single implementation commit. expires_at is an additive optional field: old readers ignore it, new readers tolerate its absence, and no persistent data migration is required.

components.disposition: ADMIT as deterministic tests only; they own no runtime authority and encode mechanical invariants (single active, CAS single-winner, exactly-once fenced settlement, real-time expiry).
evidence: Thread hammer (8 threads x 25 rounds through separate FleetStore file descriptors) and a 6-process subprocess hammer both assert exactly one active lease and monotonic generations.
TTL tests use real sleeps and real wall-clock expiry, no patched clock.
The coordinator-boot TOCTOU was first observed as this suite's begin_run race test deadlocking; the fix moved find-or-create under one lock.
components.verification_level: Focused suite plus adjacent fleet gates and full non-real_llm pytest
components.model_evidence_veto_recovery_exit: Tests expose exact mechanical behavior and can be revised independently of production state.
components.rollback_route: Revert together with the implementation if the tranche is abandoned.

components.disposition: ADMIT as exact changed-path coverage and submitter declarations; A.5 remains a mechanical presence/coverage gate.
evidence: Manifest partitions the exact base-to-candidate changed-path set and declares the single control component.
components.verification_level: Local exact A.5 self-gate before any publication
components.model_evidence_veto_recovery_exit: Human/model review remains authority for classification truth and promotion.

g1.necessity: Round-1 lease lifecycle could violate its own single-authority invariant under real concurrency: a two-phase reclaim left phantom active generations, acquire silently stacked on a live lease, coordinator boot raced on project creation, and no expiry fact existed so an over-due lease could never be recycled mechanically - each hole forced either wrong durable state or a semantic guess by whoever recovered next.

g2.authority_owner: the existing durable fleet registry: state.json re-read under the existing cross-process fcntl lock in FleetStore
g2.non_duplication: No new store, controller, daemon, or clock authority. Reclaim/renew/reclaim_if_expired reuse the same lock, the same state file, the same lease generation fencing, and the same exactly-once settlement; ttl_seconds is a declared field on the existing WorkerLease, and expiry is computed from the existing module clock.

model_evidence: thread hammer through separate flock descriptors: exactly one active lease per workspace, monotonic generations
cross-process subprocess hammer: same invariants under real fcntl serialization
CAS recovery race: one winner lease, seven LeaseConflictError losers, loser settlement fenced
real-time TTL facts: unexpired refusal with remaining seconds, expiry pass, renewal extension, fenced renewal, expiry-free refusal
g3.recovery_or_reason: Every refusal carries its mechanical reason. Live-lease takeover without a time fact remains available only through the explicit reclaim path (operator decision), and recover() exposes expires_at/expired so a model or human can judge before acting.

g4.rollback: Revert the single implementation commit; expires_at is optional and additive, old and new state files stay mutually readable, no data migration.
verification: RED-first: suite failed against round-1 store (missing typed errors, phantom-active hammer, boot TOCTOU deadlock)
GREEN: full race/expiry suite passes on the fused implementation
adjacent fleet gates (reclaim gate, project coordinator) stay green
